## Why C?

Why does a 2026 curriculum still start with C?

> *"Why do you think a 2026 curriculum still starts with C and not Python?"*

---

## C is everywhere that matters

| System | Written in |
|--------|-----------|
| Linux kernel | C |
| CPython | C |
| SQLite | C |
| Redis | C |
| Windows kernel | C |
| macOS kernel (XNU) | C |
| Git | C |
| PostgreSQL | C |

---

## Why C — the honest reason

- **Nothing is hidden.** You allocate memory. You control how data is stored. You see what the machine does.
- **Industry.** Linux kernel · Chrome · game engines · AI inference runtimes · embedded systems.
- **Foundation.** C first → C++, Java, Go feel easy. Memory abstractions won't surprise you.

> *"C gives you great freedom — and punishes mistakes severely."*

---

## What you will be able to do by January

- Write, debug, and test programs in C/C++
- Read and understand others' code
- Apply coding style and portability rules
- Use multithreading and standard libraries
- Understand how AI frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) use C++ underneath

**External benchmark:** the course covers 100% of the CLE and 80–90% of the CLA (cppinstitute.org).

Code::Blocks · VSCodium · CMake · Doxygen · Codeforces · Diagrams.net · Far Manager · Moodle

## The 2-week cycle

```
Lecture → Practice (quiz + live-coding) → Homework (online judges)
      → admission quiz → Graded test (lab) → next topic
```

- **Slides come after the lecture.** Attendance is recorded. Write 1–2 pages in your own words.
- **Homework is not graded** — but test problems come from homework.
- **Register on Codeforces this week**, before the entrance test.

---

## Graded test rules — read carefully

| Rule | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Time | One period; lateness does not extend it |
| Phones | Forbidden |
| Screen recording | **Required for the whole session. No recording = 0 points.** Install OBS Studio, test at home. |
| Allowed resources | Course slides · cprogramming.com · ASCII table · judge platform |
| Plagiarism + AI checks | After every test |

---

## Graded test — scoring

Judge mechanics: unlimited attempts, partial credit counts.

| Score | Points |
|-------|--------|
| < 60 | 0 |
| 60–74 | 0.5 |
| 75–99 | 0.75 |
| 100 | 1.0 |

Own laptop: screen facing instructor · light theme · taskbar visible · recorder running.

---

## Grading map

| Component | Points |
|-----------|--------|
| Entrance test | 4 |
| Tests T1–T4 (12 pts each) | 48 |
| Test T5 | 8 |
| **Semester total** | **60** |
| Pass threshold | 38 |
| Exam | 40 |
| Bonus | up to 10 |

---

## Exam format

Written · ~4 hours

- 24-question test — **12 pts**
- 2–3 judged programming problems — **20 pts**
- One theory question in detail — **8 pts**

---

## Retakes — the rule that matters

- One extra attempt per test
- Retake windows: **November** (entrance, T1, T2) · **January** (T3–T5)

> ⚠️ Retaking with existing below-threshold points **zeroes the old points regardless of outcome.** Retaking is a real decision, not a free lunch.

---

## AI policy

| | Rule |
|--|------|
| ✅ Allowed | Understanding (explanations, examples) |
| ✅ Allowed | Reviewing code **you wrote** (style, structure) |
| ❌ Forbidden | Graded tests and exam |

**Responsibility:** whatever an AI proposed and you accepted is **yours** — including its bugs.

## Resources and communication

- **LMS course** "Программирование (2026-2027)": tests · gradebook · theory · coding-style guide · judge links
- **Optional companion:** "Programming practicum" — homework/test walkthroughs + mock tests

## Questions?

Common questions:

1. *"What if I miss a graded test for a valid reason?"* → Same retake rule; one attempt, November/January.
2. *"Can I use C++ features?"* → Per-topic requirements state what's allowed; style rules always apply.
3. *"Are video recordings enough instead of lectures?"* → No — auxiliary and partly outdated; attendance is recorded.
